label: mid-prefix step (t=3-6) after j/t/e/v context in r/h/i-initial sequences
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.02% of steps) that fires almost only during the original phase at steps 3-6 (peak at t=4), plus the <DEL> step (12% of mass); it is essentially silent in the copy phase and at t<3. Firing is enriched when several weak factors line up: the first token is r (15x lift; h and i about 5x), the previous one or two inputs are j/t/e/v, and the current input is q/3/s/r/c/h. No single factor is close to sufficient, and the activation looks like a soft conjunction over a hidden-state code. The strict 4-way conjunction gets dev F1 0.28 (P 0.32, R 0.25); looser versions raise recall to about 0.6-0.75, but precision drops to under 6%. Top activations (about 0.19-0.2) occur when most of these factors hold together, e.g. r ? j t [x]. No coherent predicate reaches usable F1.
